source_text: Generatio autem, quae coepit ab Adam, et post legem permanet; quae si esset fons peccatorum et frutex diaboli, sicut tu argumentaris, non utique usque ad legem, sed et post legem et post Christum hoc crimen vigeret. Peccatum itaque, de quo Apostolus pronuntiat, quia usque ad legem fuerit nec potuerit manere post legem, actionis, non nativitatis esse convincitur.
pass_a_gloss: But generation, which began from Adam, remains even after the law; which if it were a fountain of sins and a shrub of the devil, as you argue, this crime would certainly not flourish until the law, but even after the law and after Christ. The sin therefore about which the Apostle pronounces that it was until the law and could not remain after the law is convicted to be of action, not of nativity.

lemmas.lexica: LS generatio; Blaise vs imitatio in Rom 5:12
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: But generation, which began with Adam, remains after the law too. If it were the fountain of sins and the devil’s shrub, as you argue, this crime would certainly flourish not only until the law but after the law and after Christ. Therefore the sin of which the apostle declares that it existed until the law and could not remain after the law is proved to belong to action, not birth (Romans 5:13).

choices.why: Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
